column2: this hybrid specimen and player remain unmeasured. Onogi, Yokoyama and Iida 2021 (Acta Acustica 5, 11; DOI 10.1051/aacus/2021003), Table 1 and section 3.1, measured one near-mf player on an isolated approximately 880 Hz head joint: reference-jet y/h = 0.24 +/- 0.25, h = 1.2 +/- 0.1 mm, angle 39 +/- 2 degrees. The offset is calculated from photographed geometry and a jet direction measured without the head joint; it excludes subsequent deflection by the instrument. Positive y/h places the reference jet outside the edge. The table's flow rate was adjusted to the human sound, not independently measured, and is not imported. The 2023 simulated 0 to 0.37 span remains a sensitivity interval, not a measured default. The cards carry this single player's value (ruling 7521, ledger onogi-yokoyama-iida-2021-flute-jet): labium offset +0.29 mm on the pipe side (y/h 0.24 x h 1.2 mm; bracket -0.01 to +0.59 mm, both ends rendered) and jet angle 0, because the 39 degrees are already inside the reference-jet offset
column3: this player unknown; external single-player reference y/h [-0.01, 0.49], not a population or specimen bound

column2: the lip jet's transfer function (amplitude and phase against Strouhal number) at the flute's Strouhal range (0.01 to 0.04) and Reynolds range (1000 to 2500): not measured. Measured planar-jet data exist only at Str_h 0.05 to 1.1 and Reynolds about 200 (de la Cuadra 2005): c_p / U_j 0.3 (long channel) to 0.5 (short), alpha_i h about 0.15 to 0.35, displacement in phase with the acoustic velocity; and for a recorder head (Price et al. 2015) an effective jet gain of about 1.6 to 3.5 against the authored 90. The island's band has one parameter that sets both its high-pass and low-pass corner, so it cannot represent a measured response; a lip-jet card from published parameters (theta / b 1.75, c_v 0.4) places its peak at the played Strouhal number, not at the measured amplification peak, and does not stage

column2: the lip covers the hole from the player's side: the cards solve it as a rigid cover on the head's outer cylinder that leaves the open strip against the hole's far edge, the edge the jet strikes (`lip one-sided`, fs-bem's wall window solved over the whole arc). Against a centred cover of the same open width it renders D4, G4 and A5 3.3, 4.2 and 8.0 cents flat (predicted 3.3, 4.3 and 8.1 on the solved loads); the image bracket it replaces (about twice the centred constriction, -19 to -50 cents) overstated it. Still unknown: the lip's edge is a straight line along the bore lying on the outer surface, where a real lip's edge is curved and stands off the surface by the lip's thickness (u-player-face), and whether the strip reaches the far edge exactly

column2: the player's face around the hole: the cards carry it as a rigid half-plane through the bore's axis, normal to the jet, rising from the outer surface 1.8 mm behind the lip's edge along the whole head (`face 0.0018`: Fletcher 1975 p.235's fitted dead interval, inside his 1 to 2 mm of p.234), solved in the window's exterior. Its static mass reaches the voice through the window's computed mass; the radiation resistance stays the bare cylinder's. With the one-sided lip, D4, G4 and A5 render 10.8, 15.0 and 21.3 cents flat of the centred cards (2 mm: 10.4, 14.4, 20.5; 1 mm: 13.0, 18.2, 25.4), and the head's end correction at f0 becomes 32.3, 33.6 and 37.8 mm (bore-referenced, from the prediction mirror on the solved loads), against about 28.8 mm without a flutist and 43 to 60 mm with one (Vauthrin 2015, eq. 2.13, Fig. 2.17). Check, not an input: at the lip's edge the solved face adds 0.81 to 0.93 of the inertance Ernoult 2018's inclined-plane law gives (eq. 24, p.13). Unknown: the face's angle (not measured for a player, Ernoult 2018 sec. 5.1 p.15), curvature and extent, the lips' opening in it, the lip's thickness and front surface, and the chin; with the lip plate (u-lip-plate) they hold the remaining 10 to 20 mm of end correction, worth tens of cents flat
column3: setback [1e-3, 2e-3] m (Fletcher 1975 p.234), a 2.5, 3.7 and 4.9 cent span at D4, G4 and A5; the face's angle, shape and extent unbounded
column5: absolute pitch, the embouchure's radiation and the radiated directivity
column6: a head impedance measured with a player (Vauthrin 2015 method), or the face's profile from photographs as the exterior obstacle

column2: the blowing pressure reaches the voice as a staircase at the cards' control rate, 1000 Hz: fs-scenario samples the gesture once per control tick and the voice holds that value until the next. A 50 ms onset ramp arrives as 50 steps, the first jumping from 0 to 1/50 of the target pressure, and the 10.5 ms release as about 10, the last dropping to 0. A finer rate is refused (MagentaBadger, Agent Mail 8043: 2000 and 4000 Hz on recorder a1 and whistle D5, 48000 Hz on recorder f1 and a1, whistle D5 and G5 and flute G4): a smooth ramp passes through pressures of a fraction of a Pa, where the jet is slower than its convection history allows, and the voice refuses rather than run outside its domain. A real breath passes those pressures in a few milliseconds; below some speed there is a slow viscous flow and no convected jet. The cards stay at 1000 Hz until the jet has a stated state below its lowest valid speed
column5: onset and release claims: speaking time, the attack transient and any line at 1 kHz; no finer rate renders, so the staircase's own effect on the attack cannot be A/B tested
column6: a jet with a stated state below its lowest valid speed (no jet below a stated threshold speed, or a convection history sized for the slowest jet the gesture reaches); then the cards move to a fine control rate with their controls budget raised

column2: the duration of the blowing-pressure onset ramp is authored and uncited: every flute card opens with `event 0e0 5e-2 pressure-pa <target>` (D4 300 Pa, G4 600 Pa, A5 379 Pa), a 50 ms rise, and closes with a 10.5 ms release; render.sh already lists the ramp as authored. No measured flute-player rise time of the blowing pressure is cited by the cards or the ledger. The 12.5 ms ramp the whistle and recorder cards take (OliveDove, Agent Mail 9574, ruled in 9581) comes from a ducted instrument; the flute is edge-blown by a lip jet, so applying it here would be a second analogy and the flute keeps 50 ms until a flute attack is cited. u-onset-control-staircase covers how the ramp reaches the voice (1000 Hz control ticks), not how long it should be
column5: the speaking time, the attack transient and the rise of every flute render; no render here separates the ramp's share of the rise from the loop's, so the ramp's effect on the attack is not known
column6: a measured blowing-pressure rise time of a flute player's attack (mouth or embouchure-hole pressure against time, at the register and dynamic of the card), then the three cards' first event takes that duration with a ledger row
